title: Congeners differ more in secondary sexual characters than in other parts

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Congeners differ more in secondary sexual characters than in other parts

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Secondary sexual characters are highly variable, and species of the same group differ from one another more in their secondary sexual characters than in other parts of their organisation.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: species of the same group differ from each other more widely in their secondary sexual characters, than in other parts of their organisation

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter V, “Laws of Variation”; section “Parts developed in an unusual manner are highly variable: specific characters more variable than generic: secondary sexual characters variable.”. Scope: sexually dimorphic animals, e.g. gallinaceous birds

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch05-14: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.67

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: This yields a standard comparative effect-size test and rich data exist for birds and some mammals. Secondary sexual traits and within-species variation are not comprehensively coded across animals.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Within genera or families, compare standardized among-species divergence and within-species variance for secondary sexual traits versus other morphology. Larger values for sexual traits support the claim; comparable or smaller divergence refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Public media and specimens are heavily biased toward birds and conspicuous traits.

Trait classes need comparable scaling and sampling.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Disparity of sexual versus non-sexual traits is a standard comparative statistic, and phylogenies for the relevant animals are public. The sexual-trait measurements themselves are still scattered, so existing global tables proxy only some display structures. Attention bias is a real confound and can be reduced by using predefined trait sets, which keeps the test informative for well-coded groups.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Within clades, compare evolutionary disparity in secondary sexual traits with disparity in other measured structures, using sex-specific data. Greater disparity in the sexual traits would confirm the claim; equal or greater disparity in non-sexual traits would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Showy characters receive more taxonomic attention, which inflates their apparent disparity.

Global morphology tables are mostly unsexed and omit plumage and other ornaments.

Sex-specific compilations are dense for a few groups, such as galliforms and lizards, and sparse elsewhere.
